items.rationale: In a workflow your code fixes the order of steps; in an agent the model picks the next step each time around the loop. Both can use tools.

accepted: the model skipping or reordering steps
items.rationale: When the model chooses the order it can skip or reorder a step that code would always run, and it makes extra calls doing so. Fixed code runs the same steps the same way every time.
The agent makes 5 - 2 = 3 extra calls per request; 3 x $0.002 x 100 requests = $0.60.
The order is fixed in code, so this is a workflow even though it makes model calls and uses a tool. Using a model, using a tool or taking several steps does not make a system an agent.

Only the failing-print job has steps nobody can list in advance, so the model must choose them as results come back. The other three have known steps in a known order, which a fixed workflow handles more cheaply.
Part 1 has steps that cannot be listed in advance, so the model should choose them; part 2 is the same steps every time, so code can run them cheaply and reliably.
